lens: Accessible interaction — long or difficult content
reason: This simulated expertise review finds strong public foundations: a readable, coherent Precision Instrument presentation, two clear audience actions, native inquiry fields and FAQ disclosures, a skip link, menu Escape/focus return, and large primary controls. The inspected client journey runs from services and engagement terms to the inquiry form; its supplied confirmation test intercepts delivery. Application source supports long written responses with associated guidance/errors, first-invalid-field focus, step-heading focus, wrapping review text and explicit original-resume disclosure. Public copy preserves pending client approval rather than inventing outcomes. However, discussion mode bypasses reduced motion and exposes a global Enter shortcut that conflicts with native control activation. Those concrete accessibility issues prevent agreement. This is source/capture and supplied local-test review, not observed user success or hosted acceptance.
inspected: src/app/apply/application-form.tsx (selected validation, focus and step/render sections)

findings.evidence: Deck entrance, spin, drumroll, shimmer, stamp, shake and pulse animations are declared at lines 522-566. The reduced-motion selector explicitly excludes .deck-root and descendants at 574-577. DeliberationDeck renders that root, animated cards and pulse (deliberation-deck.tsx:275,310-313,348); only the numeric count-up checks the preference.
findings.userImpact: Motion-sensitive participants reviewing a long cohort still encounter large card movement and repeated decorative motion despite requesting reduced motion. Projection does not remove this access need.
findings.suggestedFix: Include the deck in reduced-motion overrides; render static cards, headshots, status and result feedback, suppress confetti/shake, and verify navigation/reveal with reduced motion enabled.

findings.evidence: The window keydown listener excludes only INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT. Enter otherwise calls advance() or reveal(), including events from focused native buttons/links. Sorting buttons exist at 279-282 and Previous/Revisit/Next at 444-450. reveal() can call APPLY_STAGE_HASH at 227. This conflict is inferred directly from source, not reproduced in an authenticated browser.
findings.userImpact: A keyboard operator activating a focused sort, navigation or revisit control can also initiate a result reveal/application for the current applicant, making focus unreliable during consequential cohort review.
findings.suggestedFix: Ignore shortcut events originating within interactive elements and respect defaultPrevented; provide an explicit native reveal/apply button. Add a focused-control Enter regression proving that only the named control acts and no stage mutation occurs.

notVerified: No live authenticated discussion-mode, application or operator session; no shared browser or new tests run for this seat.
No assistive-technology, physical-device, Safari/Firefox, zoom/reflow or long-content task study. Captures show default public hero states, not keyboard focus, error announcements or private content.

Supplied Chromium passes cover menu focus and instrument reduced motion, not the discussion-mode conflicts identified here; synthetic contact/application responses do not prove Clerk, Supabase, storage or email integration.
No staging, deployment, human usability success, formal accessibility conformance, Board policy approval or client-approved project artifacts established.
